title: DEP 1.0 shapes and messages (draft)
description:
JSON Schema for every message, payload and resource body of the Document Editing Protocol 1.0, generated from packages/protocol/src/definition (SPK-019).
Validate a text frame against `#/$defs/Frame`, a payload against `#/$defs/<Name>`. CDM content refers to the CDM schema by its `$id` (urn:docedit:cdm:1:draft), published at spec/cdm.
No object forbids unknown members: receivers MUST ignore fields they do not know (05 §1 rule 3).

Envelope.title: Envelope
Envelope.description: Every text frame is one JSON object. Receivers MUST ignore members they do not know, and ignore message types they do not know (05 §1 rule 3).

id.description: Set by the sender on a message that expects a reply.

re.description: The `id` this message replies to. Required on every reply.

ch.description: Channel number, on every channel-scoped message including `ch.open`.

DocRole.title: DocRole
DocRole.description: A document-level role, carried in the `docs` claim (05 §3.1; 07 §2).

RegionRole.title: RegionRole
RegionRole.description: A role a region grant may give (07 §2).

Restriction.title: Restriction
Restriction.description: An output restriction from the `restrict` claim (05 §3.1; 13 §5).

ScopeId.title: ScopeId
ScopeId.description: A scope identifier: `doc`, `body`, `defs`, `region:<id>`, `story:<id>` or `field:<id>` (05 §5.3), where `<id>` is a node identifier.

FeatureName.title: FeatureName
FeatureName.description: A feature name. Protocol and CDM features share one namespace; experimental names start with `x-` (05 §1).

ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode
ErrorCode.description: A code of the error registry (05 §5.8).

holder.description: The user who holds the lease: the host's `sub` (D42).

expiresAt.description: When the lease ends unless it is extended.

active.description: Whether the participant is active in the workflow.

Access.title: Access
Access.description: Effective access, sent in `ch.opened` and as the whole payload of `perm.changed` (05 §5.5).

rev.description: Access revision of this connection; it increases whenever anything that feeds effective permissions changes.

asOfSeq.description: The sequence number whose region list this access describes.

scopes.description: Capabilities per scope. Lists every region of the document; a region not listed is not editable until an access with `asOfSeq` at or after the commit that created it arrives.

fill.description: Fill permission, or null when it does not apply (12 §4.1).

restrictions.description: Output restrictions; empty when none apply.

Step.title: Step
Step.description: A step as produced by `Step.toJSON()` of the pinned prosemirror-transform release (04 §4). Validated by the authority, not by the envelope.

stepType.description: The step type. The authority accepts only the seven known types and rejects any other with `invalid_op` (04 §4), so the wire format accepts any string.

Origin.title: Origin
Origin.description: Origin of a commit: a client hint (recorded, never trusted) or a server-reserved origin (04 §3.1).

Commit.title: Commit
Commit.description: A step commit as submitted: the payload of `sync.submit` (04 §3.1; 05 §5.3).

id.description: Commit identifier chosen by the client; reused unchanged when the same commit is resubmitted.

base.description: The `seq` the client had applied when it created the steps.

Ack.title: Ack
Ack.description: The payload of `sync.ack` (05 §5.3; 04 §7). `re` is the envelope `id` of the submit.

id.description: The commit identifier.

serverTime.description: Server time of the commit (04 G6).

rebased.description: Whether the steps were rebased. Always true for a read-restricted reader, whose acknowledgement carries the steps of its class (ADR 0019, proposed).

steps.description: The mapped steps: required when `rebased` is true; an acknowledgement rebuilt for a duplicate always carries them.

QuotaKind.title: QuotaKind
QuotaKind.description: The kind of quota a refusal names: the dimensions of the tenant quotas (06 §12; owner decision 110).

SyncReject.title: SyncReject
SyncReject.description: The payload of `sync.reject` (05 §5.3; 04 §8). A commit whose base is older than a snapshot commit gets `stale_base` with action `rebase` (04 §3.2).

id.description: The commit identifier from the submit (it may be malformed, which is why it is not typed as a UUID).

code.description: A registry code with the sync surface.

scopes.description: Scopes involved, for `permission_denied`; never a scope the reader may not see.

rule.description: The rule or constraint that failed (12 §5.3).

retryAfterMs.description: How long to wait before retrying.

quota.description: For `quota_exceeded` and a spent room CPU budget: the kind of quota reached (owner decision 110).

Author.title: Author
Author.description: Server attribution of a commit (04 G6).

user.description: The user the commit is attributed to: the host's `sub` (D42), or `system` (04 §10).

session.description: The session; null for server-authored commits.

agent.description: The assistant that acted for the user, or null (13 §6.2).

ControlChange.title: ControlChange
ControlChange.description: The change a control commit records (04 §3.2). Only `{ "type": "grants", "rev": n }` appears in the prose.

type.description: What changed (04 §3.2 lists grants revisions, region states, lease breaks, workflow transitions and participant completion).

RemoteCommit.title: RemoteCommit
RemoteCommit.description: A stored commit as broadcast in `sync.commit` (05 §5.3).

steps.description: The steps as applied; empty for a control commit. For a read-restricted reader, the steps of its class, which are empty when the commit changed only hidden content (ADR 0019, proposed).

control.description: The change a control commit records; null for a step commit.

Resume.title: Resume
Resume.description: Where a client resumes a channel (05 §5.2; 04 §9).

incarnation.description: The log incarnation the `seq` belongs to.

view.description: The `view` of the `ch.opened` the confirmed document came from (ADR 0019, proposed). Under read restrictions a missing or different token forces `catchUp: "reload"`.

Inflight.title: Inflight
Inflight.description: The fate of the in-flight commit named in `resume` (04 §9).

seq.description: The `seq` of the stored commit, when accepted.

CatchUp.title: CatchUp
CatchUp.description: How a joining client catches up (05 §5.2).

Limits.title: Limits
Limits.description: Every limit a client must respect (05 §5.1).

maxMessageBytes.description: Largest UTF-8 size of one frame; larger messages are chunked.

maxRebaseSteps.description: Most steps a commit may be rebased over (default 5,000, 04 §5).

heartbeatMs.description: Idle interval after which a side sends `ping` (default 25,000).

ackTimeoutMs.description: How long a client waits for an answer to a submit (default 15,000, 04 §8).

presenceHz.description: Most presence updates per second per client (default 10, 04 §11).

catchUpBytes.description: Most bytes streamed on resume (default 5 MiB, 04 §9).

CdmRange.title: CdmRange
CdmRange.description: A range of CDM major versions (05 §2).

id.description: The user identifier: the token's `sub` (D42).

name.description: Display name, when the token has a `name` claim.

quota.description: For `quota_exceeded` and a spent room CPU budget: the kind of quota reached (owner decision 110).

fatal.description: A fatal error is followed by the matching close code (05 §5.7).

versions.description: The server's versions, in the error before close 4406.

head.description: The durable head when the channel was attached; the first live commit is `head + 1`.

view.description: An opaque token naming the visibility class (the projection for this reader) that the content and stream of the channel belong to (ADR 0019, proposed). A client echoes it in a later resume.

WorkflowStatus.title: WorkflowStatus
WorkflowStatus.description: The workflow state and the participant's status, carried by `wf.changed` and `ch.opened.workflow` (12 §6.2, §10).

state.description: The participant's own status: `active` (may act now), `unverified` (their turn, but the access code is still to be submitted), `waiting` (an earlier order first), `completed`, `paused` (while correcting), `closed` (the workflow ended), or `copy` (a `cc` participant). Never another participant's.

Notification.title: Notification
Notification.description: The payload of `event`: "this changed; fetch it over REST if you care" (05 §5.6).

resource.description: The resource that changed, relative to `rest`.

data.description: Small data; thread events carry the thread's current range and the `seq` it refers to.

PresenceState.title: PresenceState
PresenceState.description: What a client publishes about itself (05 §5.4).

selection.description: Positions in the confirmed document at `seq`.

PresencePeer.title: PresencePeer
PresencePeer.description: A peer in `presence.state`; the server adds identity (05 §5.4).

ProblemDetails.title: ProblemDetails
ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 problem details with the `code` member (05 §6.1).

code.description: A code of the registry (05 §5.8); `status` is the code's HTTP status in the registry (D61).

violations.description: For `validation_failed`: where the body breaks which rule. Never the offending value (BE-088).

path.description: A JSON Pointer into the request body.

message.description: For a field that does not pass when a participant completes (12 §5.3): the message the document's author gave for the pattern the value does not match (12 §3.2 `validation.message`). A text of the document's definitions, never a value.

retryAfterMs.description: For `rate_limited` of the access code (FRW-039): how long to wait before retrying; `Retry-After` carries the same wait in whole seconds.

quota.description: For `quota_exceeded`: the kind of quota reached (owner decision 110).

Discovery.title: Discovery
Discovery.description: The discovery document at `{endpoint}/.well-known/dep` (05 §2). Every member listed is required; it is the same for every tenant of the endpoint and needs no token (D66).

ws.description: The WebSocket address; the subprotocol is `dep.v1`.

rest.description: The complete REST base URL; resource paths are relative to it.

exportTargets.description: The export targets the deployment offers (`pdf`, `tex`, and others by name), present when the `exports` feature is announced. A client offers these and no other; a service refuses a target that is not in the list with `validation_failed`. Absent: the deployment does not say, and a client offers the PDF and the LaTeX bundle (UX-101; ADR 0382).

jwks_uri.description: The public keys of the tokens the service mints (`POST /tokens`), so that a host can check them. Never used to verify a host-signed token, whose keys come from the tenant registration (05 §3.1).

Content.title: Content
Content.description: Document content at a `seq` (05 §6.2): the CDM envelope plus `seq` and `incarnation`.

requires.description: Features the document uses; a reader that lacks one MUST refuse it (03 §2).

doc.description: The document root, valid against the CDM schema.

view.description: The view token of the reader's visibility class that this content belongs to (ADR 0019, proposed). A client resumes a channel opened from this content with it.

CdmEnvelope.title: CdmEnvelope
CdmEnvelope.description: A CDM document as stored and transferred (03 §2).

NotificationType.title: NotificationType
NotificationType.description: Notification type: an open vocabulary; a client ignores types it does not know (05 §1 rule 3).

WebhookDelivery.title: WebhookDelivery
WebhookDelivery.description: Any webhook body: a CloudEvents 1.0 event in structured JSON mode. Requests are signed as described by Standard Webhooks: headers `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature`, HMAC-SHA256, five-minute tolerance.

id.description: Event identifier.

type.description: The event name with its version suffix, for example `dep.export.completed.v1`.

TokenRequest.title: TokenRequest
TokenRequest.description: The claims a host asks the service to mint (05 §3.1); member names are the claim names. The service sets `iss`, `aud`, `iat`, `exp`, `jti` and `tid` itself.

sub.description: Opaque, stable user identifier; hosts SHOULD NOT use e-mail addresses.

docs.description: Document identifiers (at most 20) mapped to the role in each.

agent.description: An agent identifier from `POST /agents`. The token is then an agent token (type `dep-agent+jwt`) for an assistant acting for `sub`, capped at `suggest` (05 §3.2.1; ADR 0234).

wfr.description: Role placeholders the user may fill outside a workflow, in the documents named by `docs` (12 §3.1, §13). The service writes them under the claim name the tenant configures, `wfr` by default (05 §3.1).

auth_time.description: When the host authenticated the participant (12 §7).

expiresIn.description: Lifetime in seconds; at most and by default 900 (15 minutes, 05 §3.1).

token.description: The minted user token (a JWS in compact form).

AgentRequest.title: AgentRequest
AgentRequest.description: The registration of an assistant agent (ADR 0234 A2).

name.description: What history and the review pane show for the agent, for example the name of the model.

docs.description: The documents the agent may act on; absent means every document of the tenant.

id.description: The agent identifier (`agt`) to put in `POST /tokens`.

docs.description: The documents the agent may act on; absent means all.

RevokeRequest.title: RevokeRequest
RevokeRequest.description: Ends a user's access before the token expires (05 §3.3).

sub.description: The user, as the `sub` claim names them.

doc.description: Limits the watermark to this document: the user's tokens issued before it are refused for this document only.

CreateDocumentRequest.title: CreateDocumentRequest
CreateDocumentRequest.description: Creates a document, optionally from CDM content, a template or an import (05 §6.2). At most one of `content`, `template` and `import`.

content.description: Initial CDM content: the content at seq 0 (D67). Without it the document starts empty.

template.description: A template (`POST /templates`) to instantiate (12 §9; FRW-062): the new document is a fork of the template document at `templateSeq`.

templateSeq.description: With `template`: the seq of the template document to fork at, pinned and recorded. Default: the head.

participants.description: With `template`: participants bound to the roles of the template. They are stored as the draft workflow of the new document.

roles.description: The `role_def` identifiers of the template that the person holds.

values.description: With `template`: values to prefill by field key, in the same call. All or none are applied.

import.description: An asset to import. Refused with `validation_failed` until imports exist (EXP).

externalId.description: The host's identifier; unique in the tenant (`conflict` otherwise).

DocumentResource.title: DocumentResource
DocumentResource.description: Document metadata (05 §6.2). Title, owner and timestamps live here, never in the CDM (03 §2). The ETag is the metadata revision.

template.description: Only in the answer to `POST /documents` with `template`: the template and the pinned seq the document was forked at (FRW-062).

UpdateDocumentRequest.title: UpdateDocumentRequest
UpdateDocumentRequest.description: A JSON merge patch of the document resource: a member present replaces it, `null` clears it. Needs `manage` or a service credential.

state.description: A change of state raises the grants revision and is recorded as a control commit (07 §9).

RegionEditors.title: RegionEditors
RegionEditors.description: "Who can edit" a region (05 §6.2), from the region policy, its state, its lease and the stored grants; the document roles themselves are in the hosts' tokens.

roles.description: Document roles that may edit the region by role alone (07 §4): `editor` and `owner` under `inherit`, `owner` under `restricted`; none while the region is approved.

principals.description: Principals with an `editor` grant on the region that has not expired; none while the region is approved.

leasedTo.description: The holder of a lease on the region; while it holds, only they may edit (07 §10).

leaseExpiresAt.description: When the lease in `leasedTo` expires (07 §10; PRM-048); present exactly when `leasedTo` is.

RegionInfo.title: RegionInfo
RegionInfo.description: An entry of the derived region list, computed from the content at the head (05 §6.2).

policy.description: The region policy (07 §4); `confidential` comes from ADR 0019 (proposed).

order.description: Position among the regions of the body, from 0, in document order.

RegionGrant.title: RegionGrant
RegionGrant.description: A region grant: document, region, principal, role, optional expiry (07 §1).

Grants.title: Grants
Grants.description: The region grants of a document (05 §6.2). Once a PATCH has returned, no commit can be stored under the old revision (04 G7).

rev.description: The grants revision (07 §9): every change of grants, region states, leases or the document state raises it. The ETag is derived from it.

grants.description: A JSON merge patch of the resource: the list replaces the current grants. A grant names an existing, unretired region; one grant per region and principal.

hash.description: For `approved`: the hash of the region's canonical content (07 §11).

Lease.title: Lease
Lease.description: An exclusive-edit lease: an identifier, a holder and an expiry (07 §10).

HistoryGroup.title: HistoryGroup
HistoryGroup.description: A group of commits (08 §4). Placeholder: not defined by the prose.

Version.title: Version
Version.description: A pointer to a `seq` with a kind (08 §4). No identifier is named.

DiffChange.title: DiffChange
DiffChange.description: One change of a comparison, keyed by block identifier (08 §6, from its example).

Attribution.title: Attribution
Attribution.description: Who wrote which spans, for a region or a block range (08 §7). Placeholder: not defined by the prose.

dryRun.description: Returns the comparison a restore would produce (08 §8).

RestoreResult.title: RestoreResult
RestoreResult.description: The outcome of a restore (08 §8). Placeholder: not defined by the prose.

ForkRequest.title: ForkRequest
ForkRequest.description: Forks a document. The member for "whether grants are copied" is not named.

ReadMarker.title: ReadMarker
ReadMarker.description: The caller's last seen `seq`; it only moves forward (08 §10). `commentSeq` is the last comment sequence number the caller has seen (a comment has a sequence number of its own in its document; owner decision 73); it moves forward on its own and is answered only when the request names it.

ConnectHint.title: ConnectHint
ConnectHint.description: Where a client should open its channel (06 §2.1). A hint only: it grants nothing.

url.description: The WebSocket URL to open the channel on.

node.description: The node the URL belongs to; empty when the service names no node.

source.description: Where the URL came from: the owner of the document, rendezvous routing over the live nodes, or the address of the service itself.

Activity.title: Activity
Activity.description: Changes and comment activity by other people since the caller's read marker (08 §10). Placeholder: not defined by the prose.

CommentBodyPart.title: CommentBodyPart
CommentBodyPart.description: One piece of a comment body: text, or a mention (13 §5; ADR 0417).

text.description: Typed text, shown as text and never as markup.

principal.description: The mentioned user or group, `user:<id>` or `group:<id>`. The node holds the identifier only; a name comes from the host (13 §5).

CommentInput.title: CommentInput
CommentInput.description: The body of a new or edited comment (13 §5; ADR 0417). The service raises `dep.comment.mentioned` for each mention of a new comment.

CreateThreadRequest.title: CreateThreadRequest
CreateThreadRequest.description: The room maps the range to the head and checks `comment` there (05 §6.2).

Thread.title: Thread
Thread.description: A comment thread with its comments (ADR 0417). The entity tag of `GET /threads/{tid}` is the `If-Match` of a change of state or assignee.

assignee.description: The person the thread is assigned to as a task, `user:<id>`; null when nobody (07 §12).

target.description: A range is where the text is at `baseSeq`; an empty range (`from` equals `to`) is a thread whose text was deleted (ADR 0015).

createdBy.description: The author of the thread and of its first comment, `user:<id>`.

etag.description: The entity tag of this version, as `GET /threads/{tid}` sends it in `ETag`: a list item has no header of its own.

comments.description: The comments in the order they were made, without deleted ones.

assignee.description: A principal, `user:<id>`, or null to clear.

ReactionCount.title: ReactionCount
ReactionCount.description: One reaction of a comment with the people who made it (ADR 0424).

users.description: The people who reacted, `user:<id>`, in the order they reacted.

Comment.title: Comment
Comment.description: A comment of a thread (ADR 0417). Its entity tag is the `If-Match` of an edit.

editedAt.description: Null while the comment was never edited.

etag.description: The entity tag of this version, the `If-Match` of an edit or delete; a comment inside a thread has no header of its own.

reactions.description: Present when the service announces the feature `reactions`; a reaction nobody holds is left out (ADR 0424).

AssetUpload.title: AssetUpload
AssetUpload.description: An asset identifier and a size-bound pre-signed upload into a quarantine area (05 §6.2). Placeholder: not defined by the prose.

locale.description: Default: the document's language (`settings.lang`), else `en-GB`. The job records the value it used.

timeZone.description: An IANA zone name. Default `UTC`. The job records the value it used.

layout.description: What the compile reports of the layout (09 §7.1). `lines` asks for line starts, for page-break reconciliation in the page view (L1); it is refused with `forbidden` unless the tenant has enabled page-break reconciliation, which is off by default (06 §10; BE-051). Default `blocks`.

target.description: A target the server does not support is refused with `validation_failed`.

seq.description: Defaults to the head when the request is accepted; above the head is `validation_failed`.

options.description: `options.suggestions` is required when the document has unresolved suggestions (`pending_suggestions`). Passed to the job unchanged.

ExportResult.title: ExportResult
ExportResult.description: The result of a completed export (09 §9.1). Warnings are in the job's `diagnostics`.

url.description: A short-lived signed URL of the output, issued after the permission check of the request that returned it (10 §3.7).

pages.description: The page count; null for a target without pages.

layout.description: A signed URL of `layout.json` (09 §11); null when there is none.

converged.description: Whether page references converged; null for a target without pages.

log.description: A signed URL of the raw compile log: only for the requester, and only while they have `edit` (09 §9.2; 07 §12).

chainHead.description: The hash-chain head of the exported state, as in the export's manifest, so that a host can anchor it (08 §12); null when the log has no commit at that `seq`.

imagesWithoutAlt.description: The number of images and figures without alternative text in the exported content, one per occurrence (09 §13). Each is also a diagnostic with the code `image_without_alt` and its block. Absent when the worker does not report it (a target that is not typeset).

ExportJob.title: ExportJob
ExportJob.description: An export job (05 §6.2; 09 §9.1). It belongs to its requester: only they, and service credentials of the tenant, may read or cancel it (review SR-C4).

seq.description: The content exported: the `seq` asked for, or the head when the request was accepted.

progress.description: Per cent done, from the worker; null while unknown.

error.description: Why the job failed, when `state` is `failed`.

ImportJob.title: ImportJob
ImportJob.description: An import job; it returns warnings on completion (05 §6.2). Placeholder: not defined by the prose.

FontManifest.title: FontManifest
FontManifest.description: Font manifest: families, styles, file URLs, hashes, licences, manifest version (05 §6.2). Placeholder: not defined by the prose.

WebhookSubscription.title: WebhookSubscription
WebhookSubscription.description: A webhook subscription: event filters, secret rotation, test ping, replay (05 §6.2). Placeholder: not defined by the prose.

AuditEntry.title: AuditEntry
AuditEntry.description: An audit entry (13 §10). Placeholder: not defined by the prose.

SearchResult.title: SearchResult
SearchResult.description: A search result (13 §10). Placeholder: not defined by the prose.

RetentionPolicy.title: RetentionPolicy
RetentionPolicy.description: A retention policy (08 section 11; 13 section 10; UX-080).

mode.description: keep_all keeps every commit payload (the default); thin_payloads keeps only checkpoints after afterDays.

afterDays.description: Days after which commit payloads are thinned. Required with thin_payloads and refused with keep_all.

RetentionView.title: RetentionView
RetentionView.description: A document retention policy with the effective policy (UX-080).

policy.description: The policy the document carries, or null when it carries none.

effective.description: The policy that applies: the document policy, else the tenant policy, else keep_all.

source.description: Where the effective policy comes from.

HistoryVisibilitySetting.title: HistoryVisibilitySetting
HistoryVisibilitySetting.description: A history visibility setting (08 section 9; HIS-025).

setting.description: editors: people with edit somewhere see full history and the rest named versions only (the default). all: everyone with view sees full history. since_access: history from the state current when the person was given access.

HistoryVisibilityView.title: HistoryVisibilityView
HistoryVisibilityView.description: A document history visibility setting with the effective one (HIS-025).

setting.description: The setting the document carries, or null when it carries none.

effective.description: The setting that applies: the document setting, else the tenant setting, else editors.

source.description: Where the effective setting comes from.

AuditSegment.title: AuditSegment
AuditSegment.description: A log segment for third-party verification (08 section 12; HIS-037).

from.description: The first seq held, not below the caller gate.

head.description: The head of the segment: the last seq and that record hash.

commits.description: The hashed metadata of each record, its payload hash, the link to the previous hash and its own hash.

anchors.description: The anchor records whose seq lies in the range.

instructions.description: How to verify the segment offline.

SuggestionIntroduction.title: SuggestionIntroduction
SuggestionIntroduction.description: The commit that introduced a suggestion (08 section 14; HIS-042).

time.description: The server time of the introducing commit, ISO 8601 UTC.

user.description: The user who introduced it, as `sub`.

origin.description: The origin of the introducing commit.

agent.description: The agent identifier when the commit was made on an agent connection (UX-046).

agentName.description: The registered display name of that agent, for example the model; absent when the agent is no longer registered.

seq.description: The seq of the introducing commit; absent when it lies below the caller gate.

TenantKeyView.title: TenantKeyView
TenantKeyView.description: A registered public key of a tenant (UX-077; 05 section 3.2).

use.description: user keys verify user tokens; service keys verify service credentials.

thumbprint.description: The RFC 7638 thumbprint of the public key.

issuer.description: The iss the key verifies, or null.

jwk.description: The public key. Private material is never registered.

KeyList.title: KeyList
KeyList.description: The public keys registered for a tenant (UX-077).

keys.description: The keys of the tenant: user keys, then service keys.

OriginList.title: OriginList
OriginList.description: The allowed origins of a tenant (UX-077; 05 section 4).

origins.description: The origins the tenant allows, in order.

KeyRegistration.title: KeyRegistration
KeyRegistration.description: The public key a tenant administrator registers (UX-077; 05 section 3.2).

kid.description: The key identifier, unique within the tenant.

use.description: user keys verify user tokens; service keys verify service credentials.

alg.description: The algorithm the key verifies; symmetric and other algorithms are refused.

jwk.description: The public key as a JWK. A key with private members is refused.

issuer.description: The iss the key verifies, or null for any.

OriginRegistration.title: OriginRegistration
OriginRegistration.description: An origin a tenant administrator allows (UX-077; 05 section 4).

origin.description: An origin: scheme, host and optional port.

QuotaSettings.title: QuotaSettings
QuotaSettings.description: The quota values of a tenant; a dimension is null when no value is set (UX-078; 06 section 12).

connections.description: Connections a tenant may hold at once.

openDocuments.description: Documents a tenant may have open at once.

commitRate.description: Commits a tenant may make in one window.

roomCpuBudget.description: Room CPU milliseconds a tenant may spend in one window.

exportConcurrency.description: Export jobs a tenant may run at once.

exportMinutes.description: Export minutes a tenant may use.

id.description: The tenant identifier, as the control plane assigns it.

name.description: The name the operator gave the tenant.

state.description: A suspended tenant is refused at the door; its data is kept (UX-076).

createdAt.description: When the tenant was registered (RFC 3339, UTC).

TenantRegistration.title: TenantRegistration
TenantRegistration.description: The body that registers a tenant (UX-076).

name.description: The name of the new tenant.

TenantUpdate.title: TenantUpdate
TenantUpdate.description: The fields of a tenant an operator may change (UX-076).

UsageView.title: UsageView
UsageView.description: The usage of a tenant in one calendar month, UTC (UX-076; decision 69).

month.description: The calendar month, UTC, as YYYY-MM.

connections.description: The most connections held at once in the month.

openDocuments.description: The most documents open at once in the month.

commitRate.description: The most commits made in one window in the month.

roomCpuBudget.description: The most room CPU milliseconds spent in one window.

storage.description: Storage used at the end of the month, or now for this month.

exportConcurrency.description: The most export jobs run at once in the month.

exportMinutes.description: Export minutes used in the month.

SealingKeyView.title: SealingKeyView
SealingKeyView.description: A PDF sealing key of a tenant, public facts only (UX-076).

alg.description: The algorithm the key signs with.

thumbprint.description: The thumbprint of the certificate that carries the public key.

HoldRequest.title: HoldRequest
HoldRequest.description: The body of a legal hold (UX-080; 08 section 11; 13 section 10).

reason.description: Why the document is held. Trimmed; at most 500 characters.

Hold.title: Hold
Hold.description: A legal hold on a document (UX-080; 08 section 11; 13 section 10).

id.description: The hold identifier.

reason.description: The reason the hold was placed with.

placedBy.description: The actor who placed the hold.

placedAt.description: When the hold was placed, ISO 8601 in UTC.

BundleExportRequest.title: BundleExportRequest
BundleExportRequest.description: The body of a bundle export (UX-087, UX-088).

kind.description: A discovery export (a document, some documents or the tenant, with the evidence) or a tenant export (everything the tenant owns).

documents.description: The documents a discovery export covers; absent, it covers the whole tenant. A tenant export names none.

maxDocumentsPerPart.description: How many documents one part holds; the service has a default.

BundleExport.title: BundleExport
BundleExport.description: A bundle export: a job that writes the parts of a discovery or tenant bundle (UX-087, UX-088).

documents.description: How many documents the bundle covers.

counts.description: What the bundle holds, to compare with the stored data.

url.description: A short-lived signed URL of the part (a tar archive).

TenantFontRequest.title: TenantFontRequest
TenantFontRequest.description: A font file and its licence declaration (BE-048).

filename.description: The file name, for the administrator only.

mime.description: The declared type of the file.

licence.description: The licence declaration the administrator makes for the file.

serverUse.description: Whether the licence allows the font on a server, so in a PDF. A font without it is shown on screen only and replaced in the PDF (decision 62).

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the file, lower-case hex.

family.description: The family name the font file declares.

format.description: The format found in the file.

serverUse.description: Whether the declaration allows server-side use.

url.description: Where the file is read, with a credential of the tenant.

TenantFontFile.title: TenantFontFile
TenantFontFile.description: The file of a font a tenant added (BE-048).

ErasePersonRequest.title: ErasePersonRequest
ErasePersonRequest.description: The body of an erasure of a person (HIS-038; 08 section 13).

sub.description: The host's `sub` of the person to erase. Hosts SHOULD NOT use an e-mail address as `sub` (05 section 3.1).

ErasePersonResult.title: ErasePersonResult
ErasePersonResult.description: What an erasure of a person did (HIS-038; 08 section 13).

outcome.description: `erased`: the mapping, the display name and the read markers are deleted. `deferred`: a document the person wrote in is under legal hold, so the erasure waits for the release (owner decision 38).

TombstoneRequest.title: TombstoneRequest
TombstoneRequest.description: The body of a tombstone of one commit payload (HIS-040; 08 section 13).

reason.description: Why the payload is removed. Trimmed; at most 500 characters. Recorded in the audit trail.

TombstoneResult.title: TombstoneResult
TombstoneResult.description: What a tombstone removed and which copies remain (HIS-040; 08 section 13).

seq.description: The commit whose payload was removed.

removedAt.description: When the payload was removed, ISO 8601 in UTC.

copies.description: The copies that may still hold the removed text; they are not rewritten.

checkpoints.description: Checkpoints at or after the commit, built by replaying it; they may still hold the removed text.

coldSegments.description: Object keys of the cold segments whose range covers the commit.

attributionMap.description: The attribution map may still name runs of the commit.

involves.description: What removing those copies involves, in fixed words.

FieldInfo.title: FieldInfo
FieldInfo.description: A field in the derived list (12 §3.2; FRW-060).

assignee.description: A `role_def` identifier, or null for a field only authors set.

values.description: Values by key, as stored (decimal strings stay strings, 12 §3.3). Placeholder name.

Workflow.title: Workflow
Workflow.description: The workflow resource, from the example of 12 §6.1; which members are required is not stated.

firstViewedAt.description: When the participant first opened the document (12 §6.3; FRW-031).

activatedAt.description: When the participant last became active: the anchor of the reminders (FRW-034).

verifiedAt.description: When a correct access code was submitted for the participant (FRW-039).

BulkSendRow.title: BulkSendRow
BulkSendRow.description: One recipient row of a bulk send: what a document made from the template takes (FRW-063).

participants.description: The recipient's participants, bound to the roles of the template.

values.description: The recipient's values, prefilled by key.

templateSeq.description: The seq of the template document to fork at. Default: the head.

rows.description: One document is made for each row, in order.

BulkSendRowResult.title: BulkSendRowResult
BulkSendRowResult.description: The outcome of one row of a bulk send (FRW-063).

index.description: The position of the row in the request, from 0.

document.description: The document made for the row; null when it failed.

error.description: Why the row failed: the code and the violations the single call would have answered.

BulkSend.title: BulkSend
BulkSend.description: A bulk send: a job that makes one fork of a template for each recipient row (12 §9; FRW-063).

seq.description: The seq of the template the documents are forked at: pinned and recorded.

rows.description: Each row with the new document or the failure; set when `state` is `completed`.

Template.title: Template
Template.description: A template: a document with role placeholders, fields and rules, and no participants (12 §9; FRW-062). The members are the lane's proposal (docs/adr/0406-w4-FRW-062-templates.md).

document.description: The document that is the template.
The document to mark as a template.

reason.description: Why the workflow is stopped: the participant who declines, or the owner who voids, says. A reason that is blank after trimming is refused.

WorkflowAccessCode.title: WorkflowAccessCode
WorkflowAccessCode.description: The body of `verify` and of the registration of an access code (12 §6.1, §7; FRW-039).

code.description: The access code: registered by the host for a participant, and submitted by the participant to verify. It is never stored or returned in the clear.

WorkflowConsentText.title: WorkflowConsentText
WorkflowConsentText.description: The consent text and the participant’s acceptance of it (12 §6.1, §8.1 step 1; FRW-044).

textId.description: The identifier of the consent text the workflow names.

text.description: The text the service holds for that identifier and version, to be shown in full before any signing action.

acceptedAt.description: The server time of the acceptance on record for this very text (ISO 8601), or null when the participant has not accepted it.

WorkflowCaptureSettings.title: WorkflowCaptureSettings
WorkflowCaptureSettings.description: The tenant setting for network identity capture in workflow evidence (12 §7; FRW-042).

captureNetworkIdentity.description: Whether the IP address and the user agent of a participant are recorded in their evidence. On by default; off keeps neither (12 §7). A change applies to events after it; evidence already stored is not rewritten.

WorkflowPlaceholder.title: WorkflowPlaceholder
WorkflowPlaceholder.description: A workflow request or response the prose does not define. Placeholder.

token.description: The user token (a JWT, 05 §3.1). Tokens are never placed in URLs.

session.description: A new identifier for every connection; there is no session resumption.

of.description: A fresh identifier shared by the chunks of one message.

part.description: A substring of the serialised message, split only between Unicode code points.

cdm.description: The CDM version the client will use.

token.description: A token for this channel; same `tid` and `sub` as the session (05 §3.1).

cause.description: Why the server closed the channel. `access_changed`: what the reader may see changed (ADR 0019), so the client reopens without `resume`; the others say why a room stopped serving, and the client resumes as for `unavailable`.

message.hello.title: hello envelope
message.hello.description: `hello` (client to server): Opens the session. Must be the first message, within 10 seconds.

id.description: Required: the message expects a reply.
Set when the sender expects a reply.

re.description: The `id` of the message this one answers.

message.auth.expiring.title: auth.expiring envelope
message.auth.expiring.description: `auth.expiring` (server to client): Sent about 60 seconds before `tokenExp`.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

message.auth.refresh.title: auth.refresh envelope
message.auth.refresh.description: `auth.refresh` (client to server): Presents a new token; with `ch`, a token for that channel.

id.description: Required: the message expects a reply.

message.auth.ok.title: auth.ok envelope
message.auth.ok.description: `auth.ok` (server to client): Reply to `auth.refresh`: the refreshed token is accepted.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

re.description: The `id` of the message this one answers.

message.auth.revoked.title: auth.revoked envelope
message.auth.revoked.description: `auth.revoked` (server to client): The session was revoked; followed by close code 4401.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

message.ping.title: ping envelope
message.ping.description: `ping` (either direction): Sent after `heartbeatMs` without sending anything; the peer answers `pong`.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

d.description: No payload members; may be omitted (D02).

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

re.description: The `id` of the message this one answers.

d.description: No payload members; may be omitted (D02).

message.goaway.title: goaway envelope
message.goaway.description: `goaway` (server to client): The whole connection is draining; never used for a single channel.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

message.error.title: error envelope
message.error.description: `error` (either direction): A typed error; with `re` when it answers a message. A fatal error is followed by the matching close code.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

re.description: The `id` of the message this one answers.

message.chunk.title: chunk envelope
message.chunk.description: `chunk` (either direction): One part of a message whose UTF-8 size exceeds `maxMessageBytes`; chunks of one message are sent consecutively; reassembly times out after 10 seconds.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

message.ch.open.title: ch.open envelope
message.ch.open.description: `ch.open` (client to server): Opens a document channel. Without `resume` the server answers with `catchUp: "reload"`.

id.description: Required: the message expects a reply.

message.ch.opened.title: ch.opened envelope
message.ch.opened.description: `ch.opened` (server to client): The channel is attached; `head` is the durable head at that moment.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

re.description: The `id` of the message this one answers.

message.ch.rejected.title: ch.rejected envelope
message.ch.rejected.description: `ch.rejected` (server to client): The channel could not be opened.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

re.description: The `id` of the message this one answers.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

d.description: No payload members; may be omitted (D02).

message.ch.closed.title: ch.closed envelope
message.ch.closed.description: `ch.closed` (server to client): The server closed a channel, for example `forbidden` after revocation, `unavailable` when the room moves or is fenced, `slow_consumer`. Under read restrictions (ADR 0019, proposed) a change of access that hides or reveals content also closes the channel with `unavailable`, and the next open reloads.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

message.sync.submit.title: sync.submit envelope
message.sync.submit.description: `sync.submit` (client to server): Submits a commit. The envelope `id` correlates the reply; the payload `id` identifies the commit.

id.description: Required: the message expects a reply.

message.sync.ack.title: sync.ack envelope
message.sync.ack.description: `sync.ack` (server to client): The commit is stored; sent only after every commit with a lower `seq` on the channel.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

re.description: The `id` of the message this one answers.

message.sync.reject.title: sync.reject envelope
message.sync.reject.description: `sync.reject` (server to client): The commit was refused; `action` says what to do next and `head` is the current head.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

re.description: The `id` of the message this one answers.

message.sync.commit.title: sync.commit envelope
message.sync.commit.description: `sync.commit` (server to client): Stored commits, in ascending `seq`; the next message continues at the last `seq` plus one.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

message.sync.caughtUp.title: sync.caughtUp envelope
message.sync.caughtUp.description: `sync.caughtUp` (server to client): The catch-up stream is complete; live commits follow.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

message.sync.reset.title: sync.reset envelope
message.sync.reset.description: `sync.reset` (server to client): A snapshot commit was stored; the client reloads content at `seq`.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

message.sync.check.title: sync.check envelope
message.sync.check.description: `sync.check` (server to client): The SHA-256 of the canonical form of the document at `seq`, for divergence detection (04 §13).

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

message.presence.update.title: presence.update envelope
message.presence.update.description: `presence.update` (client to server): Publishes the client's selection; positions refer to the confirmed document at `seq`.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

message.presence.state.title: presence.state envelope
message.presence.state.description: `presence.state` (server to client): Peers and sessions that left. The server adds identity and MAY drop or coalesce presence under load.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

message.perm.changed.title: perm.changed envelope
message.perm.changed.description: `perm.changed` (server to client): A complete new `access` object. The server enforces it from the moment it computes it.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

message.perm.changed.$comment: 05 §5.5; gaps: G44, G46, G103; decisions: D12

message.event.title: event envelope
message.event.description: `event` (server to client): "This changed; fetch it over REST if you care."

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

message.wf.changed.title: wf.changed envelope
message.wf.changed.description: `wf.changed` (server to client): The workflow state and the participant's status; sent like `perm.changed`.

id.description: Set when the sender expects a reply.

Frame.title: Frame
Frame.description: One text frame: the envelope, checked against its message type when the type is known. A frame of an unknown type is valid here and is ignored by the receiver (05 §1 rule 3).
